correctness.rationale: The character pairing \(\operatorname{tr}(AB)\) is nondegenerate in odd characteristic. For every nonzero frequency \(B\), the rank-one character sum is \(qZ(B)-(q^2+q+1)\), and the rank-two sum is evaluated by binary full-rank character transforms over all two-planes. The four exact pairs \((S_1,S_2)\), ordered by rank one, split rank two, anisotropic rank two and rank three, are \((-1,q^2(q-1))\), \((q^2-1,q^3-2q^2)\), \((-q^2-1,q^3)\), and \((-1,-q^2)\). The ternary quadratic Gauss-sum identity is derived in the proof, not assumed without justification. The first three powered-distance multipliers are strictly below \(-1\) for all positive powers; the rank-three multiplier \(-1+q^2(3^t-2^t)\) has one positive zero. Fourier diagonalization and double-centering give the exact negative-type interval and minimum Euclidean dimension. The rank-three stratum has exactly \(q^2(q-1)(q^3-1)\) frequencies. Complete FFT experiments at prime orders three, five, and seven match every nonzero frequency, but the proof itself covers all odd prime powers.

value.rationale: The metric is a natural global invariant of the \(q^6\)-point geometry of ternary symmetric bilinear forms for every odd finite field. The theorem gives a sharp negative-type boundary, the unique representation-theoretic sector responsible for losing exactly \(q^2(q-1)(q^3-1)\) Euclidean dimensions at the endpoint, and a universal \(q^{-2}\) asymptotic law. Unlike a pre-existing character table or a small numerical census, it proves simultaneous strict sign inequalities across split and anisotropic spectral sectors for all odd prime powers. Determining sharp Hilbert embeddability of rank-metric geometries is a specific mathematical motivation; characteristic two and larger symmetric matrices are not claimed.
